purpose: Agent quick validation selection for common Clawix changes without real services.
measurementNotes: Measured locally with warm caches and a 15s per-check timeout.
Timings are advisory; the runner prints fresh timings on every run.
The current scripts/test.sh fast lane contains 131 run commands before Swift package and web tests, including 35 self-tests, 44 UI checks, and 39 governance-like checks.

checks.detects: tracked generated or ignored artifacts entering review
checks.failureAction: Remove the tracked ignored artifact or update ignore policy with a documented reason.

checks.detects: bloated or divergent always-loaded agent instructions
checks.failureAction: Move procedure detail into routed docs or skills and keep AGENTS.md as a router.

checks.detects: missing or stale constitutional assertion coverage
checks.failureAction: Update the assertion manifest or the referenced canon in the same change.

checks.detects: Clawix mirror drift from shared constitutional canon
checks.failureAction: Synchronize the mirror text or route the decision through the shared canon.

checks.detects: missing accessibility surface coverage and expiring accessibility gaps
checks.failureAction: Add surface coverage, capability evidence, or an expiring gap with owner and repair path.

checks.detects: bridge contract drift between app-facing surfaces and protocol expectations
checks.failureAction: Update the contract, fixture, or consumer on both sides of the boundary.

checks.detects: stale generated surface-route registry entries
checks.failureAction: Regenerate or correct the route registry and include the source change that explains it.

checks.detects: surface evidence projection drift
checks.failureAction: Update the projection baseline or fix the surface evidence that changed unexpectedly.

checks.detects: broken localization guard behavior before app-source scanning
checks.failureAction: Fix the guard fixture or detector before relying on localization results.

checks.detects: new visible string localization debt across iOS, Android, and Web
checks.failureAction: Move visible strings into the platform localization resource or update the approved baseline.

checks.detects: native permission broker policy drift
checks.failureAction: Route sensitive permissions through the signed host broker and update the allowlist or docs.

checks.detects: native action broker allowlist or ownership drift
checks.failureAction: Keep native actions brokered by the signed host and update the registered action surface.

checks.detects: broken persistent-surface detector behavior
checks.failureAction: Fix detector fixtures before trusting app-source persistent key results.

checks.command: node scripts/persistent-surface-guard.mjs macos ios android windows web/src linux/app/src
checks.detects: unregistered persistent keys and native permission identifiers
checks.failureAction: Register the persistent key/native permission surface or remove the unregistered literal.

checks.detects: new expensive work on hot UI or runtime paths
checks.failureAction: Add boundedness metadata or move expensive work off the hot path.

checks.detects: unbounded loops, lists, scans, and baseline debt in high-churn paths
checks.failureAction: Add concrete limits, windows, cursors, or an approved expiring baseline entry.

checks.detects: missing UI implementation evidence manifests and required public checks
checks.failureAction: Update the UI evidence manifest and attach the required public validation commands.

checks.detects: broken heavy markdown rendering detector fixtures
checks.failureAction: Fix detector fixtures before accepting markdown rendering changes.

checks.detects: source naming and file-shape drift
checks.failureAction: Rename, split, or document exceptions according to the naming and source-shape canon.

checks.detects: large source files crossing reviewability thresholds
checks.failureAction: Split the file, update an intentional baseline, or justify the generated/registry exception.

checks.detects: stale code-hygiene inventory and audit summaries
checks.failureAction: Refresh the hygiene audit artifacts or fix the stale inventory source.

checks.detects: invalid package public-surface shape
checks.failureAction: Keep public package surfaces explicit and aligned with package ownership.

changeTypes.label: Agent instructions or routed docs
escalateTo: scripts/test.sh fast when instructions alter public policy

changeTypes.label: Constitution, ADR, release, or governance policy
escalateTo: scripts/test.sh fast for broad canon changes
scripts/test.sh release only for release work

changeTypes.label: Bridge, route, protocol, Relay, or surface graph
escalateTo: scripts/test.sh integration for macOS bridge/runtime changes

changeTypes.label: Native permissions, approvals, grants, or host actions
Visible UI, localized copy, or UI evidence
escalateTo: platform unit tests for changed client
real app validation for visible macOS bugs

changeTypes.label: Performance-sensitive UI/runtime path
escalateTo: real trace/profile before claiming performance validation

changeTypes.label: Package, source shape, or hygiene inventory
escalateTo: relevant SwiftPM, Vitest, or platform unit tests for functional code

changeTypes.label: Web app surface
escalateTo: npm --prefix web test when dependencies are installed

knownRedundancies: Fast currently runs many governance checks and their self-tests on every change; self-tests mainly validate the checker, not the product change.
UI governance checks dominate the fast lane even when no UI surface changed.
Release readiness and external-pending checks run in fast even though their natural home is release or goal closure.
Inventory scans such as naming, source size, code hygiene, and persistent surface app scans are useful but should be selected by changed paths instead of always blocking the shortest agent loop.
missingCoverage: No public quick selector maps changed paths to recommended checks before this matrix.
The changed lane chooses mostly between fast and integration; it does not explain why a check is needed for a common change type.
Several failures print detector-specific lines but do not provide a next action in one place; this matrix adds failureAction text for the quick runner.
Web and mobile checks rely on dependency availability or device hooks; the quick suite keeps local static checks separate from those external prerequisites.
